title: Commit adds a node_modules symlink to an absolute host path
detail: 7d9bd9a adds node_modules as a symlink (mode 120000) to /home/claude/danizee-claude-suite/node_modules; .gitignore only ignores node_modules/ so the link got through; dangling in every other clone and exposes the host path
fix_hint: git rm --cached node_modules; ignore node_modules without the trailing slash

title: An untracked path git cannot diff exits 1 and is dropped silently, so a failure can become 'no change to review'
detail: git diff --no-index exits 1 both for differences and for some errors (an untracked nested repo: error Could not access 'sub/null', exit 1, empty stdout); only code>1 is a failure, so diff-range exits 3 and --json lists the path under untracked with empty:true
fix_hint: treat code 1 with empty stdout or non-empty stderr as a failure; list a path in untracked only when its diff text is non-empty

title: Command text still says any non-zero exit is a failure although the blocks exit 3 for an empty range
detail: the graph paragraph never mentions exit 3 and says a non-zero exit is a broken state; the lens and impact paragraphs say the same right after the exit-3 sentence; same text in the regenerated w-review.md
fix_hint: say 'any non-zero exit other than 3 (empty range)' in all three paragraphs and add the exit-3 sentence to the graph paragraph

title: The impact block calls diff-range twice and the --base advice covers only one call
detail: the diff and the base-only call can be given different bases and nothing notices
fix_hint: resolve the base once into B and pass --base $B to both diff-range and impact, or say the ref goes on both calls

title: Non-UTF-8 file content is rewritten as U+FFFD in the printed diff
detail: defaultGit decodes stdout as utf-8, so a latin-1 byte becomes EF BF BD and the diff no longer matches the file
fix_hint: read the diff calls' stdout as a Buffer and let raw be a Buffer that cli.js writes undecoded

title: An untracked symlink to a directory makes the whole verb exit 1
detail: git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <link> follows a symlink to a directory and fails exit 1 with 'Could not access <link>/null'; the exit-1-with-stderr rule then throws, so lenses, graph and impact all stop with diff-range failed; a .gitignore line node_modules/ does not match a worktree's node_modules link (reproduced on git 2.43)
fix_hint: lstat each untracked path first; for a symlink build the added-file diff from the link target text (mode 120000) instead of following it; add a test with a symlink to a directory

title: When the merge base fails with an upstream set, the range silently becomes the whole history
detail: when @{upstream} resolves but merge-base fails (exit 1 in a shallow clone, or 128), the code falls through to the empty tree with no error, so every tracked file is reported as the change (reproduced with a --depth 1 clone)
fix_hint: with an upstream and no merge base, exit 1 with 'no merge base with <upstream> (shallow clone?): pass --base'; keep the empty-tree fallback only for no upstream

title: --base refuses the empty-tree id that --base-only prints in a SHA-256 repository
detail: --base-only prints hash-object -t tree /dev/null (6ef19b41... in a sha256 repo) but --base accepts only the hard-coded SHA-1 constant, so the w-review blast-radius block always fails there (reproduced with git init --object-format=sha256)
fix_hint: compare f.base with the repository's own hash-object -t tree /dev/null result instead of the SHA-1 constant

title: The blast-radius block ignores a failed --base-only and reports a misleading second error
detail: nothing checks the first call's exit status; when it fails B is empty and the second call fails with '--base needs a ref', which misleads the diagnosis (nothing is skipped: the step still exits non-zero)
fix_hint: test [ -n "$B" ] (or || { echo 'diff-range --base-only failed' >&2; (exit 1); }) before the second call

title: Any stderr warning on an untracked-file diff aborts the whole range (core.autocrlf / eol=crlf)
detail: exit 1 with any stderr text is treated as failure; with core.autocrlf=true git prints a benign 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' warning for every LF text file while the diff on stdout is correct (confirmed on git 2.43), so every untracked text file fails the range on those setups
fix_hint: run the --no-index diff with -c core.safecrlf=false, or treat only stderr lines not starting with 'warning:' as failure; add a test with core.autocrlf=true

title: Hand-written symlink diff header does not quote paths as git does; a newline in the name injects diff lines
detail: the symlink block writes the raw name in 'diff --git' and '+++' lines; git C-quotes names with quotes, backslashes, control chars or newlines (and non-ASCII under core.quotePath) and adds a TAB after a name with a space; a symlink named with an embedded newline split the header and parseDiff read a path that does not exist
fix_hint: quote the name as git does (C-style quoting, TAB after ---/+++ names with a space), or skip-and-report an untracked symlink whose name has a newline; add tests with a space, a quote and a newline

title: diff-range runs programs and can fetch over the network when the reviewed repo's .git/config says so (textconv, clean filters, fsmonitor, lazy fetch)
detail: defaultGit only sets core.hooksPath=/dev/null and strips GIT_*; a planted .git/config with diff.X.textconv, filter.X.clean and core.fsmonitor ran all three programs during diff-range (markers created), textconv output replaced the real content the lenses read, and a blob:none partial clone fetched missing blobs from the promisor remote with the user's credential helper; the header claims a hardened read
fix_hint: apply safe-git's overrides to both diff calls: --no-textconv, -c core.fsmonitor= -c diff.external= -c credential.helper= -c protocol.allow=never and GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 in env (a missing blob then exits 1 with a clear message); state the remaining trust assumption in the header

title: --ignore-submodules=all makes a committed submodule pointer bump disappear (exit 3)
detail: a superproject pointer bump with --base HEAD~1 prints nothing and exits 3; with a hostile submodule config, --ignore-submodules=dirty printed the pointer change and ran no program, while none ran the submodule's clean filter
fix_hint: use --ignore-submodules=dirty on both diffs (the flag overrides diff.ignoreSubmodules=all); test a pointer bump in range with a planted filter not running; update the header

title: An include.path in the untrusted repo's config is followed with no timeout: a FIFO hangs the verb forever
detail: mkfifo .git/inc + git config include.path inc made git config -z --list block forever; defaultGit uses spawnSync with no timeout; safe-git uses --no-includes and a timeout on every child
fix_hint: pass a timeout to every git child and exit 1 on expiry with a plain message, and/or read the config with --no-includes (then includes are data not followed); name the remaining gap in the header

title: Many driver names overflow GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS: E2BIG with a jargon error
detail: 600 filter sections make spawnSync fail with E2BIG (128 KiB single env string cap); it fails closed but the message says nothing useful
fix_hint: put per-driver pairs on argv as -c options (as safe-git does) and keep only the statics in the env, or exit 1 with 'too many filter/diff/merge drivers configured (N) to switch off safely'

title: Partial-clone error text is nested and jargon-heavy with no runnable next step
detail: the message nests parentheses two deep and uses promisor/GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH/transports without a command
fix_hint: one plain sentence with a command: this is a partial clone and some file contents are not downloaded; diff-range never downloads; run git -C <dir> diff <base> >/dev/null once, or use a full clone

title: No test checks that every git call carries the hardened env or that an inherited GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is replaced
detail: the planted-config test proves the programs do not run during the diffs but no test records the env per call; a future call through the unwrapped runner would pass the suite
fix_hint: add a recording fake around defaultGit asserting every call's env has the overrides, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1, and that a caller's GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is dropped

title: Include refusal reads only --local, so an include in the per-worktree config (config.worktree) is followed and its filter driver runs
detail: with extensions.worktreeConfig=true git also reads $GIT_DIR/config.worktree, which --local does not cover; a filter defined in a file included from config.worktree is never found by the --no-includes driver read but the diffs follow the include (reproduced: PWNED created, exit 0); the header claims nothing named in any config git reads is executed
fix_hint: read git config --list -z --no-includes --show-scope once and refuse include.path/includeIf.*.path in scope local or worktree; add a test with a config.worktree include

title: Header says nothing from any config git reads is executed, but drivers defined in files the user's global/system config includes are not switched off
detail: the driver list comes from --no-includes, the diffs follow global includes; the header contradicts itself
fix_hint: narrow the sentence: drivers defined in files your own global/system config includes are yours and are not switched off

title: Any signal death is reported as a timeout
detail: with a timeout set, r.signal && !r.error turns any signal (OOM SIGKILL, SIGPIPE, external kill) into the 'took longer than N ms' message
fix_hint: use the timeout message only for r.error?.code === 'ETIMEDOUT'; report other signals as 'git <cmd> was killed by <signal>'

title: Partial-clone note asserts 'this is a partial clone' on any matching error and its command is not runnable for paths with spaces
detail: the MISSING regex also matches a corrupt full clone's 'bad object'/'unable to read'; the suggested git -C ${dir} is unquoted
fix_hint: say 'if this is a partial clone' (or check remote.*.promisor / extensions.partialClone) and single-quote the dir

title: /w-review does not name the refused case (exit 2) diff-range can now return
detail: exit 2 is reachable (an include in the repo config, a bad driver name) but the text says any other non-zero exit is wrong input or a broken state
fix_hint: append: exit 2 means diff-range refused the repository (e.g. an include in its own config): report the refusal as printed; regenerate w-review.md

title: Include refusal message gives an unclear remedy
detail: 'run the read through safe-git' names no command and safe-git does not produce this range
fix_hint: say: remove the include from .git/config (git config --local --unset include.path) and run diff-range again

title: One hardened git process per untracked file, with no cap and no overall time bound
detail: 2,000 one-line untracked files took 8.4 s (4.2 ms each); 50,000 would take minutes, w-review runs it three times, --timeout bounds each child only, no --max-untracked and no count in the output
fix_hint: diff all untracked files in one process: temp GIT_INDEX_FILE copy, git add -N -- <files> with the same overrides, one git diff <base>; or cap the count, list the rest in skipped and print a note

title: Output over 64 MiB fails with an unnamed ENOBUFS, and no size cap matches downstream's 32 MiB limit
detail: a 70 MB untracked log gives 'kit: cannot run git: spawnSync git ENOBUFS' with no path or remedy; a 50 MB range passes diff-range but graph/impact refuse it (maxDiffBytes 32 MiB); the range is held three times in memory
fix_hint: map ENOBUFS to a message naming the command, output size and (in diff-range) the untracked path; lstat untracked files and put any above a byte cap in skipped with reason too_large; refuse a total above graph's maxDiffBytes with a clear message

title: Header and a test title still say the partial-clone failure names that lazy fetch is off
detail: the message now says diff-range never downloads; the header line and the test title at test/kit-diff-range.test.js:370 still claim the lazy-fetch wording
fix_hint: change both to 'naming the missing object and that diff-range never downloads'

title: Merged add -N diff pairs a deleted tracked file with an untracked copy as a rename, so the content disappears
detail: a tracked old.txt moved by hand to untracked new.txt printed only rename from/to with no hunks; the --no-index fallback printed a delete plus a full add; the two paths differ and lenses/graph see no content
fix_hint: add --no-renames to the diff (both paths) so an intent-to-add file is always a new-file entry; test both paths on a hand-moved file

title: In a sparse checkout an untracked file outside the cone makes the whole verb exit 1
detail: git add -N refuses paths outside the sparse-checkout definition; that stderr does not match the fallback regex, so the verb exits 1 with a mislabelled 'cannot list the untracked files' error; the fallback works
fix_hint: pass --sparse to add -N (an older git without it already takes the fallback) and relabel the error 'cannot add the untracked files to the temporary index'

title: A range whose only changes were skipped by the caps exits 3, which w-review reports as no change to review
detail: a repo whose only change is a 9 MB new file exits 3 with only a stderr note; same with --max-untracked 0; the header's own rule says an unread untracked path is never exit 3
fix_hint: when the diff is empty but skipped holds max_untracked or too_large entries, exit 1 naming the skipped files; test a single oversized new file

title: With core.splitIndex on, add -N on the temporary index writes a new sharedindex file into the real .git
detail: one run left a new .git/sharedindex.<sha>; the verb writes to a repository it claims only to read
fix_hint: run the add and the diff with -c core.splitIndex=false

title: An unconditional --sparse sends git 2.25-2.33 to the per-file fallback on every run
detail: git add --sparse shipped in 2.34; older gits reject it as unknown option and always take the --no-index loop; before 2.34 add -N ignores the cone anyway
fix_hint: pass --sparse only when the config read shows core.sparseCheckout=true, or retry add -N once without --sparse before the per-file fallback

title: Fallback regex matches any stderr that contains 'sparse' or 'usage:'
detail: a real add -N failure mentioning a path with 'sparse' quietly switches to the slow path and the real cause is never reported
fix_hint: anchor on git's option-parse failure only: /unknown (option|switch) `(sparse|pathspec-from-file|pathspec-file-nul)/ or exit 129 with usage:

title: Usage and header give exit 3 / exit 1 for empty and cap-only ranges, but --json exits 0 in both
detail: with --json no exit is returned; nothing names the --json exit code or says to read empty and skipped_detail; no test covers the cap-only --json case
fix_hint: add '(--json: always exit 0; read empty and skipped_detail)' to usage and header; add one assertion on the cap-only --json result

title: An unreadable untracked file fails the whole verb as 'cannot diff against the base'
detail: a mode-000 untracked file makes the merged diff exit 128 and the message points at the base, not the untracked file
fix_hint: label a failing merged diff 'cannot diff the range (tracked changes plus N untracked files)'

title: The --sparse retry never runs on a real git 2.25-2.33 because git's usage text lists --pathspec-from-file
detail: the retry requires !/pathspec-/ on the whole stderr, but git prints the full add usage after the error line and that usage names --pathspec-from-file; so the per-file fallback is taken instead; the tests fake stderr without the usage body
fix_hint: test only the first error:/fatal: line of stderr for both the sparse match and the pathspec exclusion; add a usage body with --pathspec-from-file to the fake stderr in the tests

title: When TMPDIR is unwritable the run fails with a bare EACCES although the per-file path needs no temp folder
detail: fs.mkdtemp is not wrapped; a read-only /tmp fails the verb as soon as any untracked file exists
fix_hint: catch the mkdtemp/copyFile failure and fall through to the per-file path, or raise a KitExit naming TMPDIR

title: The usage line describes --json too narrowly and says it always exits 0, which the code does not do
detail: skipped also holds too_large and max_untracked entries; under --json the code still exits 2 for an oversized range or a config include and 1 for failures
fix_hint: say skipped/skipped_detail cover nested repositories and cap-skipped files, and --json exits 0 whenever a summary is printed; errors and refusals keep 1/2

title: An unreadable real index is reported as a TMPDIR failure
detail: copyFile sits in the same try as mkdtemp, so an EACCES/EIO on .git/index prints 'cannot create a temporary index in <tmpdir>'; the per-file output is still correct
fix_hint: name the failing step in the note (create a temporary index / copy the index)

title: TMPDIR fallback test covers only mkdtemp ENOENT, not a copyFile failure or temp-dir cleanup
detail: no test makes mkdtemp succeed and copyFile fail and checks that no diff-range-index-* dir is left
fix_hint: add a case with a writable TMPDIR where the copy fails and assert no leftover temp dir

title: callers --symbol: exit 0 with a `missing` symbol or `partial: true` is not covered
detail: caller-floor.js run() returns exit 0 with NO entry for a symbol whose file was not read, whose name is not in the file, or whose path does not exist: the symbol goes to `missing` with a reason, and `partial`/`not_read` are set. The step never mentions `missing`, `partial` or `not_read`, so a symbol with no entry reads as 'no callers' on a normal input (typo, renamed file, unread or too-large file).
fix_hint: Add: 'Exit 0 can still leave a symbol out: read `missing` (each with its reason) and `partial`/`not_read`; a symbol in `missing` was not answered, never "no callers".'

title: Receipt is recorded before Compound and leaves out untracked files, so push-gate check will not match the reviewed change
detail: The receipt is keyed on sha256(base, tree); the tree is HEAD plus tracked changes only (status --untracked-files=no, add -u). The closing step runs before Compound, which writes docs/solutions/ideas/<name>.md, and the build's new files are usually still untracked. Once committed, the HEAD tree differs from the receipt tree and push-gate check asks or denies.
fix_hint: Say to stage new files (git add -N or git add) before the receipt and to re-record after Compound if it changes tracked files; or move the receipt after Compound. State that untracked files are not part of the receipt.

title: Exit 2 explained only for diff-range; the lenses, graph and impact refusals and the --base-only refusal are mislabeled
detail: graph and impact document exit 2 refused but the step names exit 2 only as a diff-range refusal; diff-range also refuses on a range over 32 MiB. In block 3 a refusal from diff-range --base-only prints 'base was not resolved' and forces RC=1, so the exit 2 is lost.
fix_hint: Name exit 2 for each verb as 'refused: report as printed', and in block 3 keep the --base-only exit code instead of forcing RC=1.

title: scrub --worktree does not scan the new untracked files that the build just created
detail: The text says 'tracked files' but reads exit 0 as clear to commit. New files from the TDD build are untracked until added, so a secret in a new file passes this step.
fix_hint: Tell the reader to git add -N the new files before scrub --worktree, or say untracked files were not scanned.

title: push-gate check exit codes not named
detail: The step tells the user to run push-gate check but not what its exits mean: 0 abstain or ask (read decision), 2 deny, 1 error. Exit 0 could be read as approved.
fix_hint: Add one sentence: exit 0 = abstain or ask (read decision), 2 = deny, 1 = error; none is an allow.

title: Other copies of the /w-plan-tdd-swarm description still say 9 phases
detail: The template now says all 12 phases, but src/utils/shortcuts.js:454 and WORKFLOW-SHORTCUTS.md:442 still say 'Use TodoWrite first with all 9 phases'.
fix_hint: Update both descriptions to 12 phases, or drop the count.

title: diff-range exit 0 with skipped files is read as a complete range
detail: diff-range exits 0 and still prints the diff when it has left untracked files out (too_large over 8 MiB, max_untracked over 20000 files, or a nested repository), writing a note to stderr and listing them in skipped_detail. Nothing tells the agent an exit-0 range can be missing files, so lenses/graph/impact run on an incomplete range and the agent can write 'nothing else is affected' about files never in the diff.
fix_hint: Add one sentence: on exit 0, read diff-range's stderr; any skipped file (too_large, max_untracked, nested repository) was not analysed, so name it and treat every result as a floor. Add a test assertion.

title: Exit-code paragraph contradicts itself on exit 2
detail: 'Any other non-zero exit is wrong input or a broken state: report it, never skip the step' covers exit 2, while a later sentence says exit 2 is a refusal: stop that step. Two instructions for one code.
fix_hint: Say 'Exit 1 is wrong input or a broken state: report it, never skip the step', and keep exit 2 in its own sentence.

title: Empty-range path ends the block with status 3
detail: When diff-range exits 3, each block prints 'no change to review' then ends with (exit $RC), so its status is 3; the Bash tool shows a non-zero status as an error although the prose says exit 3 is never a failure.
fix_hint: In the 3) branch set RC=0 after the echo, or say that status 3 from the block is expected.

title: Missing kit is reported as a diff-range failure
detail: The blocks never check that .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js exists; when missing, node exits 1 and the block prints 'diff-range failed (exit 1)', which the prose says to report as a broken state, conflicting with the advisory fallback. A failing mktemp is reported the same way.
fix_hint: Start each block with [ -f .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js ] || { echo "kit missing: skipped (advisory)"; exit 0; } in a form that does not kill the shell.

title: push-gate check exit 2 is not always a deny
detail: check also exits 2 through a KitExit when the receipt store is refused (a symlink at or inside the receipts folder). That is a refusal of the store, not a deny decision about the change.
fix_hint: Say 'exit 2 deny (read decision and reason) or a refused receipt store (kit: refused: on stderr)'.

title: Skipped-file instruction asks for names the block output does not show
detail: A nested repository is listed only in skipped_detail (--json only, and none of the blocks passes --json; no stderr note). The max_untracked stderr note gives counts only, never names. An agent following the text literally must guess or drop the requirement.
fix_hint: Say that max_untracked prints only a count (report the count) and that nested repositories are visible only with diff-range --json (skipped_detail); or name each file only where stderr names it.

title: A failed mktemp is reported as 'diff-range failed (exit 1)'
detail: When mktemp is missing or TMPDIR unwritable, D is empty and the redirect fails before node runs; the block prints 'diff-range failed (exit 1)' although diff-range never ran. Fails closed, but the diagnosis names the wrong tool (all three blocks).
fix_hint: Guard the temp file: D=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$D" ] || { echo "mktemp failed: no temp file for the range" >&2; RC=1; } before calling diff-range.

title: Splitting the exit codes dropped the catch-all for codes other than 0-3
detail: The new text names only exits 0-3. A verb exit such as 127 or a signal (134/137) has no documented meaning for lenses, graph or impact.
fix_hint: Add: 'Any other non-zero exit (for example 127, or a signal) is a failure of that step: report it, never read it as nothing found.'

title: Range temp file is left behind if a block is interrupted
detail: The three Code Analysis blocks write the full diff-range output (which can include an untracked .env) to a mktemp file removed only by the trailing rm -f; no trap, so an interrupt during graph or impact leaves the copy in TMPDIR (mode 0600). Same pattern as the existing w-review blocks.
fix_hint: After mktemp succeeds add trap 'rm -f "$D"' EXIT INT TERM, or run the mktemp-to-rm part in a subshell with that trap.

title: Redact skipped in a linked worktree although the verb would find the secrets
detail: The block checks .claude/kit/secrets relative to the cwd and, if missing, writes the text as is. redact.js secretsRoots() looks in the worktree top and then the main checkout's .claude/kit/secrets (the file is git-ignored, so a linked worktree normally has no copy). Streams run in linked worktrees, so on that path the raw diff, with any real secrets, goes into the solution doc or memory export, which Phase 2 commits. Same when the cwd is a subdirectory.
fix_hint: Drop the shell existence check and always run redact --keep-lines when the kit is installed (with no secrets file the verb returns replaced 0), or check the same roots the verb checks.

title: A git diff failure in the redact pipeline is read as an empty, clean result
detail: In `git diff HEAD~1 | node ... redact --keep-lines; RC=$?`, RC is redact's exit only. If git diff fails, redact reads empty stdin and exits 0 with text ''. Reproduced with HEAD~5 on a 2-commit repo. The block also fixes the input to git diff HEAD~1 although the prose says any excerpt.
fix_hint: Write the diff to a temp file first and check git's exit code, then redact --keep-lines < file; or pipefail in a subshell and report PIPESTATUS.

title: 'abstain (no receipt)' is wrong: with no receipt, push-gate check returns ask
detail: push-gate.js decide(): a change with no receipt goes to block(), which returns ask at threshold none and deny at any other threshold, reason 'no review recorded for this change; run /w-review before pushing'. Abstain only comes from a passing receipt or an incomplete one that found nothing blocking. So every /bcp without a prior /w-review lands on ask and does not push, which contradicts the stream spec (no receipt → the push goes on) and would make the gate blocking. test/w-background-compound-command.test.js:74 asserts the wrong wording.
fix_hint: Say abstain = a passing or incomplete-but-clean receipt; state that no receipt returns ask with reason 'no review recorded…' (threshold none) or deny (stricter --threshold); for that one ask reason the push goes on and the summary says 'no review recorded, pushed'; any other ask is not pushed.

title: The background agent has no way to put an ask to the owner
detail: Phase 3 runs inside the autonomous background agent. On ask it is told to put the question to the owner, but a background agent cannot hold a conversation with the owner and nothing tells the lead to relay the ask or resume the push.
fix_hint: On ask, the agent stops and puts the gate's reason in the Phase 4 summary as 'not pushed — gate asks: <reason>'; the lead relays that to the owner and runs the push in the foreground only after they answer.

title: The merge-to-main push is not covered by the gate decision
detail: The gate checks the current branch's HEAD tree against its upstream merge-base. The step then merges into main and pushes main, a different change that is never checked.
fix_hint: Run push-gate check again on main after the merge and before pushing main, or state that the gate covers only the branch push.

title: A refused lead commit leaves the handoff files staged, and the agent's commit is not path-limited
detail: On a refused lead scrub the handoff files stay staged and dispatch still happens; Phase 2 'Commit with descriptive message' names no pathspec, so the lead's staged files would go into the agent's commit. Phase 2 exit 1 and other exits do not say 'skip Phase 3'.
fix_hint: Agent commits with git commit -- <its paths>. After a refused lead scrub: unstage and do not dispatch, or dispatch without --push. Add 'skip Phase 3' to Phase 2's exit 1 and other-exit clauses.

title: No test runs a block with the kit installed, and one temp dir leaks
detail: Tests only match wording and run blocks with no kit present; nothing runs push-gate check, scrub --worktree or the redact pipeline against a real repo. nodeMk() creates a temp dir never removed; an import sits mid-file.
fix_hint: Add a fixture repo with the kit copied in and assert the real decision, exit code and redacted text for each block. Remove the temp dir in finally; move the import to the top.

title: Redact block diffs the lead's handoff commit, not the session's work
detail: CHECKPOINT 1 commits the handoff files before the agent is dispatched, so the agent's `git diff HEAD~1` covers the handoff commit plus uncommitted edits, not the session's committed work. After a refused handoff scrub there is no handoff commit and the same line gives a different range. The real diff never goes through redact unless the agent improvises.
fix_hint: Have the lead record the pre-handoff HEAD (or the session's base) and pass it to the agent; diff that range in the block (git diff "$BASE"), never HEAD~1.

title: After a refused handoff scrub, the agent's scrub refuses too, so the claimed write-up commit never happens
detail: scrub --worktree scans every tracked file on disk. Unstaging only helps for a new file; a hit in an already-tracked handoff file stays on disk, the agent's Phase 2 scrub exits 2 and it does not commit, although the text promises the write-up commits.
fix_hint: Say the agent's scrub will also refuse while a tracked file holds the hit, or have the lead pass that fact so the agent skips Phase 2 and reports it. Do not claim the write-up commits.

title: Main re-check after the merge stops every reviewed change
detail: push-gate changeId hashes (merge-base with @{upstream}, HEAD tree). On main after the merge the base differs from the one the receipt was keyed on, so with any receipt decide() returns ask 'only an earlier review exists, for a different version of this change', which is not the no-review reason: a reviewed change is held while an unreviewed one goes through.
fix_hint: Have the main re-check pass --base set to the base the branch check used so a fast-forward merge of the reviewed tree matches its receipt; or document the outcome and route it to the relay explicitly.

title: Relay path loops: the lead's foreground rerun of Phase 3 stops on the same ask or deny
detail: After the owner answers, the lead runs the Phase 3 lines, push-gate block first; nothing changed, so the gate returns the same ask or deny and Phase 3 says not pushed. Read literally the owner's answer never leads to a push, and a deny is treated like an ask.
fix_hint: State that after the owner explicitly says go on an ask, the lead pushes without rerunning the gate's stop rule (the permission prompt still applies); a deny is never pushed past, the owner must fix the cause first.

title: Agent dispatched without --push after a handoff scrub refusal writes the wrong 'not pushed' reason
detail: The lead's text says the summary reads 'not pushed — handoff scrub refused', but the agent is dispatched without --push and Phase 3 writes 'not pushed — owner's go needed (/bcp)', misleading when the owner ran /bcp.
fix_hint: Have the lead put the reason into the agent's dispatch prompt, or write the line itself; make clear which.
